ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a carbonyl structure can be seen; there is a double bond between the central carbon and the oxygen atom on the right, and the central carbon is also connected by single bonds to two substituents labeled R¹ and R², respectively. At the lower left there is an independent H3N (ammonia) species, shown with a lone pair. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, what actually needs to be encoded is a carbonyl fragment and a separated ammonia molecule. R¹ and R² are unspecified substituents, represented by wildcard atoms * in SMILES, so the carbonyl fragment is *C(*)=O. H3N, as a separate ammonia species, can be written as N. The two fragments are not connected, and are connected with a dot, giving *C(*)=O.N.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and list only the actual atom labels and solid/double bonds, explicitly discarding the curved arrows. Convert the carbonyl fragment as a carbon atom double-bonded to O and single-bonded to two unspecified R groups, giving '*C(*)=O'. Then encode the separate H3N species as 'N' and join the disconnected fragments with a dot, yielding '*C(*)=O.N'.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the single natural route: directly transcribe the non-arrow structural skeleton in the image into SMILES. There are no genuinely independent numerical or textual derivations; the answer depends on recognizing the drawn functional groups and applying SMILES notation.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the depicted atoms and bonds while ignoring all curved arrows: a central carbonyl carbon double-bonded to oxygen, single-bonded to two generic substituents labeled R1 and R2, plus a separate ammonia/nitrogen species H3N with a lone pair shown nearby and no ordinary drawn bond to the carbonyl carbon.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that asks for the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and specifically says to ignore the arrows, so electron-flow arrows should not create extra SMILES bonds or charges.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: generic R substituents can be represented as wildcard atoms '*'; a ketone/aldehyde-like carbonyl skeleton with two generic substituents is '*C(*)=O'; disconnected components are separated by '.'; ammonia can be written as 'N' when hydrogens are implicit. Curved arrows indicate electron movement and are not encoded as bonds when the prompt says to ignore arrows.
